summary: San Dimas Peak lookout (1917) was burned in 1919; the later cabin moved to the LA County Fairplex in 1992; the summit is closed except by permit.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 30 foot K-brace steel tower (register); the Angeles Adventures history describes a 14 by 14 foot wood cab
facts.status_note: The cabin moved in the early 1990s and was rebuilt at the Los Angeles County Fairplex in Pomona in 1992; a radio site with a 100-foot tower is listed on the original summit

staffing.status: last observer Sandy DeLapp in the 1950s; closed 1955 and decommissioned because of smog pollution

access.note: The original summit is in the San Dimas Experimental Forest, technically closed to the general public except under special written permit (Angeles Adventures). The Fairplex display is open during the Los Angeles County Fair.

facts.agency: Angeles National Forest (original builder and site); Los Angeles County Fairplex administers the cabin today

notes_for_editor: Five sources read. The 1992 Fairplex move date and the 2019 NHLR registration of the Fairplex record (Nov 2, 2019) are in the sibling record us-ca-johnstone-peak-at-la-county-fairplex and are not repeated here. The scrn.net listing is undated, so the radio-site claim is the least certain line. The summit's status is from Angeles Adventures and scrn.net; no source read describes any remains of the lookout on the summit. A peakery user log quoting a 'No entry without a permit' sign was seen but not cited. Record coordinates (34.16011, -117.79978) match the NHLR original location.
